concrete_scene.heading: Worked proof-transport trace: one receipt, two consumers
concrete_scene.actor_or_system: A pinned Circle RoPE receipt presented to a structural diagnostic and an architecture-promotion consumer
concrete_scene.attempted_action: Determine whether the same theorem-linked receipt may support finite position bookkeeping and a claim of better trained-model context behavior.
concrete_scene.observable_outcome: The diagnostic accepts the bounded theorem, field, and fingerprint contract while the architecture gate rejects promotion for missing workload, baseline, quality, runtime, and memory evidence.
concrete_scene.failed_or_tested_boundary: The trace tests whether theorem validity and receipt transport automatically confer empirical consumer authority; the two opposite decisions show that they do not.
concrete_scene.residual_owner: The downstream architecture evaluation owns model workload, baseline, quality, cost, failure, and adoption evidence that the proof receipt cannot supply.
concrete_scene.evidence_boundary: The ASI-side gate validates one pinned public receipt and four mutations; it does not rebuild the general Circle proof stack or establish model behavior, transfer, or deployment.

worked_trace.heading: Worked proof-transport trace: one receipt, two consumers
worked_trace.maximum_inference: The trace demonstrates consumer-specific use of a pinned proof receipt and rejection of four malformed or overclaiming variants; it establishes no general proof transport or model-performance result.

counterexample_or_simpler_baseline: The simpler verified-badge baseline treats a theorem name as architecture approval. The transport envelope instead resolves the exact receipt and asks whether the requested consumer claim lies inside its authority.
readable_claim: A proof-carrying contract lets a small formal fact travel without turning that fact into a claim about model behavior or deployment.
normative_rule: A consumer may use a formal receipt only after resolving its theorem identity, assumptions, source and toolchain, fingerprints, replay state, expiry, and non-claims. The consumer must separately justify every empirical or operational decision it wants to make from that fact.

caveat_consolidation.local_caveat: The trace keeps its local boundary to one public pinned receipt and two explicitly different consumers.
caveat_consolidation.consolidated_disposition: The complete theorem, fingerprint, replay, revocation, private-source, transport, and model-performance limitations remain in their dedicated receipt and formal sections.

bookkeeping_surface_disposition: The two-consumer table remains because the opposite decisions are the mechanism; receipt field inventories, lifecycle states, and mutation counts remain in reference surfaces.

editorial_diagnostics.mega_sentence_disposition: The new reader claim and rule make proof identity, transport, and consumer authority readable before the exact formal envelope.
editorial_diagnostics.hedge_disposition: One local scene boundary replaces no distinct limitations and keeps the general transport and empirical non-claims visible.
editorial_diagnostics.table_disposition: The compact table is argument-bearing because one receipt produces two consumer-specific decisions.

non_claims: The trace does not establish a general proof-transport service or clean external replay.
The trace does not establish model quality, runtime, memory, safety, or deployment.
The editorial revision does not move chapter-core support or release state.
